waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; shared approach for Liberty Bell and South Early Winters Spire (NW Forest Pass required).
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway, about 1 mile west of Washington Pass. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Liberty Bell Mountain
waypoints.note: First of the five summits: the traverse tops out Liberty Bell by the Beckey Route, then carries on south over Concord Tower, Lexington Tower and North Early Winters Spire to finish on South Early Winters Spire.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Blue Lake Trail about 1.5 miles to the climbers' junction just past a small stream, marked by a large cairn, then climb the path up slabs, talus and heather into the gully below the Liberty Bell-Concord notch. Keep climber's left low in the gully, cross right higher up, and take the left fork a couple of hundred feet below the notch to the Beckey Route start; four short pitches lead to the summit.

waypoints.name: Concord Tower
waypoints.note: Second summit of the traverse, climbed by its North Face from the Liberty Bell-Concord notch.
waypoints.directions: From Liberty Bell's summit, descend the Beckey Route and its rappels into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch, then climb Concord Tower's North Face to the top.

waypoints.name: Lexington Tower
waypoints.note: Third summit, climbed by its North Face.
waypoints.directions: Rappel Concord Tower's south face into the notch below Lexington, then climb Lexington Tower's North Face to the top.

waypoints.name: North Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: Fourth summit, climbed by its Northwest Corner.
waypoints.directions: Rappel Lexington's south face, cross a short but exposed 3rd-class section, make one more short rappel, and walk to the base of North Early Winters Spire. Climb its Northwest Corner to the summit.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: Fifth and last summit, finished by its Southwest Rib; descend by the South Arete rappels and walk back to the Blue Lake Trail.
waypoints.directions: Get down off North Early Winters Spire and finish the day on South Early Winters Spire by its Southwest Rib.

waypoints.name: Hairpin Turn Pullout (Hwy 20)
waypoints.note: Dirt pullout at the hairpin switchback ~0.5-1mi east of Washington Pass, directly beneath the east faces of North/South Early Winters Spire; hike up Spire Gully to the NEWS-SEWS notch, then traverse left to the route base. Parties often descend via South Arete/Blue Lake Trail and hitchhike back to a car left here.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to Washington Pass (the highway is closed over the pass in winter), then continue east, downhill, to the big hairpin switchback just below the pass; from the Mazama side it is the hairpin you reach as the road climbs to the pass. Park in the dirt pullout at the hairpin, about 5,100 ft, directly below the east faces of the Early Winters Spires. This is not the Blue Lake Trailhead.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.directions: Hike up Spire Gully, following occasional cairns, to the last large tree in the middle of the gully, then traverse right across talus (snow early in the season) until you are under the gully that climbs to the North–South Early Winters Spires notch. Traverse left to the foot of the east buttress and climb its nine pitches to the summit.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; shared approach for Liberty Bell and South Early Winters Spire (NW Forest Pass required).
waypoints.directions: The Blue Lake Trailhead is on the south side of SR 20 (North Cascades Highway) a little under a mile west of Washington Pass, between mileposts 161 and 162, about 42 miles east of Newhalem or 31 miles west of Winthrop. The paved lot is small and fills early. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is required.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: True summit of South Early Winters Spire, between Liberty Bell and Blue Lake Peak.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Blue Lake Trail about 1 to 1.25 miles to the clearing on the spire's northwest side, then take the climbers' path up talus and heather into the basin below the northwest face. Find the chockstone-filled chimney between the two formations; the route starts at the steep corner entered by a traverse, just right of the bolted Mojo Rising start. Climb six pitches to the summit.
